notes: Session 2. Closed B5-0623 on human order to finish the half-done heartbeat migration FIRST, with the run-queue.ps1:162 suffix crash queued SECOND and not yet started. The order's premise was half right and the difference mattered: measured rather than assumed, the migration was FUNCTIONALLY COMPLETE and merely uncommitted. validate-heartbeats.ps1 exits 0 at 27 files, 27 conforming, 0 non-conforming; migrate-heartbeats.ps1 -DryRun reports MIGRATE-JSON 28 with nothing outstanding; and the ten paths git shows deleted are NOT deletions but the A1.1 sanitised renames, with solar-pro4-free.json, Kiro (pi-coding-agent).json and both kilo (nvidia-nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b-free) spellings present under their new names and six non-conforming files correctly parked in _quarantine. A git status full of D entries is what made this look like data loss. The real defect was the DOCUMENT and it is the same class I reported against B5-0622: 00_BOOT.md step 3 declares HEARTBEATS/README.md binding for a schema requiring schema_version, agent_id, utc, state and live_claims, while that README was still the original 2026-09-21 file specifying four fields and NONE of the semantics, so the enforced schema existed only inside the validator and a boot-time reader obeying the document would have written pre-schema files and been rejected by a tool whose complaint pointed at a document that never mentioned the requirement. FIXED: rewrote HEARTBEATS/README.md from 22 lines to 8660 bytes as the real binding contract, including the active/idle/busy enum, the identity-resolution rule requiring agent_id to resolve to exactly one file, the three-signal liveness rule with LIVE/STALE/UNKNOWN and the explicit prohibition on returning -1, the never-parse-notes rule, and the exit-code contract, plus an explicit precedence rule that if README and validator ever disagree the validator is what runs so they cannot drift apart silently again. Also fixed two validate-heartbeats.ps1 diagnostics that still advertised the enum as only active and idle after busy was added by human approval in Amendment A1, deriving the message from $ValidState instead of retyping the literal; the tool had been silently accepting busy while telling authors it was invalid. Verified: validator exit 0, migration dry-run clean, and a field-by-field cross-check confirming README, validator and boot step 3 agree on all five required fields. Committed the entire migration INCLUDING the 00_BOOT.md step 3 pointer that the previous checkpoint deliberately left unstaged because it cited untracked files; that citation now resolves. No agent_id altered and no heartbeat renamed beyond the A1.1 set, so all 268 existing citations keep resolving. NOT DONE, human decision per Amendment A1: the opencode identity ambiguity, where this session and another write under opencode-family identities and cannot see each other, so live_claims is derived correctly and stays semantically ambiguous until one session owns one identity; no schema change fixes it. Reusable lesson: half-finished names a state, not a cause, so measure which half is missing before repairing either, because a data-migration pass here would have found nothing to do and left the only real defect in place while creating a false paper trail.
